newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 4.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
-Ministers are to be asked to agree shortly to spending cuts of up to 40 million Irish pounds in order to offset the cost of a nurses' pay deal.
- Food company Avonmore reports record pre-tax profits of 36.5 million Irish pounds to end 1996, an increase of 14 percent on previous year.
- The government is to launch action plan to address labour skills shortage as survey reveals 'recruitment problem'.
- Irish police suspect bomb left beside Sinn Fein office in Monaghan planted by loyalists.
- Tanks roll on Albanian streets as government loses control of the south.
- Irish Development Agency to offer cash incentives to industries setting up outside major urban centres.
- The petfood company set up by former Irish prime minister Albert Reynolds is to receive grant aid of 1.7 million Irish pounds.
- Irish prime minister John Bruton meets with senior EU officials to stave off multi-billion pound cuts in Ireland's structural funds.

- Irish prime minister John Bruton demands that the British government shows compassion to Roisin McAliskey who is awaiting a high court decision on her extradition to Germany to face trial over the IRA attack at Osnabruck.
- An interest rate hike of one percent possible shortly if money markets feel Ireland will fail to meet criteria for European Monetary Union (EMU).
